name: Cups slide through the crossing
aliases: naturality of the crossing for the cup
summary: A wire crossing both legs of a cup can be moved off the cup.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The cup $|00\rangle + |11\rangle$ is even, so the crossing is natural with respect to it: a wire that crosses both legs of a cup (through two fermionic crossings) can be pulled off it. The signs of the two crossings cancel.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator; bare cups cannot be drawn with ZXLive-style boundaries
